core.title: Make every visual spec compare a screenshot
core.given: An e2e test — a browser-level spec assigned to the e2e-test role by the stack's rules (its e2e-test file pattern together with the e2e runner, or a journey binding in the file header, so a misnamed file is still judged; a unit test that merely mentions a journey identifier in a string is not one) — identified as visual: it carries the stack's visual harness code in its test URN, or its file basename contains the stack's visual name token (a whole name segment, not an arbitrary substring).
core.when: The spec is evaluated (new, changed, or existing unchanged).
core.then: The spec MUST contain at least one of the stack's accepted screenshot-comparison calls.
prefer: Assert the rendered state with a named screenshot comparison.
avoid: Labelling a spec visual (test-URN harness code or file name) while it only asserts on structure or text, so it captures nothing and performs no visual regression.
Renaming the file or dropping the visual identification merely to escape this check instead of adding the screenshot comparison.
unless: The file lives in a vendored or generated tree; these are never scanned (the exact trees are the stack's single never-scanned list).
core.why: A visual spec that captures nothing performs no visual regression.
evidence: Every e2e spec identified as visual by the stack's visual identification (visual harness code in the test URN, or visual name token in the file basename) contains at least one of the stack's screenshot-comparison calls.
The stack's convention check for this rule reports no findings (strict disposition, severity 3).
verification: Strict disposition, severity 3: every finding fails; there is no advisory mode.

Visual identification is the OR of the stack's two visual markers: the visual harness code in the test URN, or the visual name token in the file basename; a name token must match exactly (a whole name segment), and name or path patterns serve only as prefilters for candidates.

Any of the stack's accepted screenshot-comparison calls satisfies the obligation; the check is call-presence only — it does not inspect what the call captures, what value it compares, or how any baseline is stored.

A file qualifies as a browser-level e2e spec per the stack's role assignment (e2e file pattern plus runner, or a journey binding in the file header); a unit test that merely mentions a journey identifier in a string does not qualify.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exact list is the stack's single never-scanned list, owned by the stack's checker.

values: e2e_test whose file basename carries the stack's visual name token (exact whole-segment token match; name patterns are prefilters only)
visual identification present (test-URN harness code or basename name token)

fires: A browser-level e2e spec carries the stack's visual harness code in its test URN but contains no screenshot-comparison call.
A spec whose file basename contains the stack's visual name token only asserts on structure or text and never captures a screenshot.
An existing, unchanged visual spec without a screenshot-comparison call is evaluated.
A misnamed test file with a journey binding and the visual identification lacks a screenshot comparison.
doesNotFire: A visual spec that contains one of the stack's screenshot-comparison calls.
A browser-level e2e spec not identified as visual (no visual harness code in the test URN, no visual name token in the file basename).
A unit test that merely mentions a journey identifier inside a string.
Files under vendored or generated trees (the stack's never-scanned list).

profileRequirements.meaning: How a test file is assigned to the e2e-test (browser-spec) role: the e2e file pattern plus runner qualification, the journey-binding alternative for misnamed files, and the exclusion of unit tests that merely mention a journey identifier in a string.
profileRequirements.bunValue: browser_spec = (a) a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright (the file-name glob alone is not sufficient; it must be a Playwright-run spec), OR (b) independently, any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// UserSystemFlow:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:userSystemFlow:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged. A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser_spec.

profileRequirements.meaning: The file-name patterns that identify an e2e test file (pattern only; whether the pattern alone suffices for role assignment is defined by roles.assignment).

The name patterns of the e2e-test (browser-spec) file kind that identify a spec as visual: a whole-name-segment token in the file basename, matched exactly (not as an arbitrary substring or path glob).
profileRequirements.bunValue: `visual`/`vis` token in the file basename (a whole name segment, not an arbitrary substring)

profileRequirements.meaning: The header syntax by which a test file binds itself to a journey, qualifying a misnamed file as a browser-level e2e spec.
profileRequirements.bunValue: header comments carry a journey marker: `// UserSystemFlow:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:userSystemFlow:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`

profileRequirements.meaning: The harness code in a test URN that identifies a spec as visual (one of the two OR'd visual markers).
profileRequirements.bunValue: a `VIS` harness code in the test URN

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's accepted screenshot-comparison assertion calls; a spec that contains at least one of them satisfies the obligation (the contract is call presence, not capture or baseline semantics).
Vendored and generated trees that are never scanned (the stack's single exclusion list).

neutralityNotes: 'Screenshot comparison' is the neutral name for the profile's accepted screenshot-comparison calls, and the core's obligation is call-presence only, exactly matching bun.json's syntactic check: nothing in the core requires capture of the rendered interface, a stored baseline, or any particular snapshotted value (core:verification records what the check does not cover). Visual identification is split per the vocabulary: the `VIS` test-URN harness code is test-identity data (urn.test_kinds#visual_harness_code) and the `visual`/`vis` basename identification patterns are file-name patterns of the e2e-test kind (suffix.e2e_test, alongside the e2e file pattern), with the OR identification semantics and whole-segment (exact token) matching retained in the core. Everything else concrete moved out of the core: the runner qualification together with the journey header markers and the unit-test exclusion (roles.assignment, urn.binding.journey), and the never-scanned trees (roots.excluded). Per-rule severity 3 and strict disposition stay in core:verification; the validator id and the needs_new_observer adapter note are Bun realization only (bunOnly). 'DOM/text' was generalized to 'structure or text'; the exact prefilter globs are Bun checker mechanics and could not be made neutral.
